T: Coffee for the coach. Orange slices for the team.
D: A mild vitamin salesman coaches his son's under-10 soccer team and gets badly hooked on coffee along the way.
P: Serve the coffee when Phil takes his first sip and the season turns.
S: the oranges every kids' team eats at halftime

Crispy chicken bites tossed in a sticky fresh orange, soy and ginger glaze, finished with sesame, spring onion and plenty of orange zest. Cut 600g chicken thigh into bite-sized pieces, toss with 1 tbsp soy, then in 60g cornflour. Fry in batches in oil at 180C for 4 to 5 minutes until crisp. Simmer the juice of 3 oranges with the zest of 1, 2 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp grated ginger and 1 garlic clove for 5 minutes, then thicken with 1 tsp cornflour in water. Toss the chicken through and top with sesame and spring onion.
Phil's vitamin shop, health first, until the coffee

Chewy oat bars packed with almonds, pepitas, cranberries and dark chocolate, bound with honey and peanut butter and cut into thick bars. Heat the oven to 170C. Toast 250g rolled oats, 80g chopped almonds and 50g pepitas on a tray for 10 minutes. Warm 120g honey, 100g peanut butter, 50g butter and 50g brown sugar until smooth. Stir into the oats with 80g dried cranberries and a pinch of salt. Press firmly into a lined 20 x 30cm tin and bake 20 minutes. Cool, scatter with 80g melted dark chocolate and cut into 12 bars once set.
M: the two Italian kids Phil recruits from the butcher shop

Grilled fennel Italian sausages in toasted rolls with charred capsicum and onion, melted provolone and a spoon of hot giardiniera. Slice 2 red capsicums and 2 onions and cook in 2 tbsp oil over medium-high heat for 12 minutes until soft and charred. Grill 8 Italian fennel sausages on a medium barbecue for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until cooked through. Split 8 long rolls, toast, and lay a slice of provolone in each. Add a sausage, the capsicum and onion and a spoon of chopped hot giardiniera or pickled chillies.
W: the coffee shop where it all starts
Crunchy almond biscotti twice-baked for dunking, the perfect thing to have with far too much coffee.
K: Phil discovers coffee and never looks back

Four shots of espresso whisked with dark chocolate and steamed milk, topped with whipped cream, chocolate shavings and a few chocolate-coated coffee beans. Melt 80g chopped dark chocolate with 2 tbsp sugar in a saucepan with 100ml milk, whisking until smooth. Add 700ml more milk and heat until steaming, whisking until frothy. Pull 8 shots of espresso. Pour 2 shots into each of 4 big mugs and top with the chocolate milk. Whip 100ml cream and spoon on, then add chocolate shavings and 3 chocolate-coated coffee beans each. Decaf is allowed.

w.how: Mix 250g plain flour, 200g sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, 3 eggs and 150g whole almonds into a dough. Shape 2 logs and bake at 180C for 25 minutes. Cool 10 minutes, slice thinly and bake 10 minutes more until crisp.
